title: Micro-OKR Runway: Rolling 6-week capacity exchange and scope auction for competing initiatives
creator: Priya Singh
description: Problem: When multiple initiatives compete for the same engineering and design capacity mid-cycle, PMs traditionally negotiate informally causing scope churn and missed OKR outcomes. Proposal: pilot a Micro-OKR Runway — a rolling 6-week capacity exchange and scoped auction where teams trade soft commit credits for guaranteed sprint-time slots. The pilot defines credits, auction cadence (weekly mini-auctions), hard vs soft commits, a fallback reserve, and measurable guardrails (latency of delivery, defect rate, and OKR attainment). Goal: reduce mid-cycle unplanned scope moves by 40% and improve predictable delivery for high-ROI work. This ticket designs rules, scorecards, tooling requirements, and rollout plan for Q2 pilot across Platform, API, and Console squads.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook describing credit issuance, weekly auction process, and hard/soft commit definitions published to Confluence
Scoring rubric for competing work (impact, customer urgency, risk, cross-team dependencies) agreed by PD and Eng leads
Prototype Google Sheet + automation template that tracks credits, auction winners, and reserved fallback slots
Pilot cohort (3 PMs + 3 Eng leads) signed up and aligned to the pilot timeline
Dashboard metric definitions for mid-cycle scope churn, auction win/loss outcomes, and OKR attainment documented
Stakeholder sign-off from Head of Product and Head of Engineering to run pilot for 6 weeks
decisions: Credits are issued per squad based on 6-week available capacity estimates (default: 8 credits per squad)
One weekly 30-minute auction conducted on Tuesday planning sync; teams can bid credits for sprint slots
Hard commit consumes 2 credits and cannot be retracted without a replacement bid; soft commit consumes 1 credit and is revocable with notice
Reserve pool: 4 credits held centrally for critical incidents or executive-prioritized work; can be allocated by product council
Tie-breaker: higher historical OKR delivery rate wins; if still tied, PM council arbitrates
comments: 2026-03-10 Priya Singh: Initial draft of Runway concept; want to avoid over-bureaucratizing planning. Putting a lightweight weekly auction is intended to create visible scarcity without heavy process overhead.
2026-03-11 Marcus Liu: Eng concern — need to ensure auctions do not lead to tokenized work that breaks sprint flow. Will prototype sheet and automation first, no infra changes required.
2026-03-11 Zoe Kaplan (Design): Suggest mapping credit cost to design touchpoints as well so design-heavy requests surface true cost. Recommend cross-discipline credits or credit multipliers.

2026-03-12 Ben Ortiz (Platform Eng): Proposed adding a "sprint affinity" label to prevent repeated bidding for low-value interrupt work. Also flagged dependency on capacity-estimate data from capacity-simulator (ENG-4682).
2026-03-12 Product Council: Approved pilot to proceed, asked PM to provide success metric targets and a rollback plan if churn increases

metrics: Mid-cycle scope moves (count per squad per 6-week window)
Auction win rate vs delivered (percentage of won slots that result in completed work within committed sprint)
OKR attainment delta for participating initiatives vs baseline
Sprint-level throughput variance (to detect churn introduced by auctions)
Number of credit disputes escalated to Product Council
